Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.6.1–13: the rakshasa in a boar's form carries her off (1.6.1); in anger the child drops (cyuta) from the womb and is therefore Chyavana (1.6.2); seeing him fallen, bright as the sun, the rakshasa lets her go and falls, turned to ash (1.6.3); Puloma takes up her son and goes on, faint with grief (1.6.4); Brahma himself sees her weeping and comforts her (1.6.5); a great river rises from her tears and follows her path (1.6.6); Brahma names it Vadhusara, by Chyavana's hermitage (1.6.7): RESOLVED, it is Brahma who names the river, and he is now named in the voice; Bhrigu sees his son and his wife (1.6.8) and asks in anger who made her known to the rakshasa, for the rakshasa did not know her as his wife, and says he will curse that one (1.6.9–10: `who`, the turn); she answers that Agni made her known and that her son's splendour freed her (1.6.11–12); Bhrigu, in great wrath, curses Agni: you shall eat everything (1.6.13, the cliffhanger). vadhu here is the daughter-in-law (Bhrigu is Brahma's son): the plaque reads "the daughter-in-law's stream". Chyavana as Shaunaka's forefather: 1.5.7–8. The CE does not say that Bhrigu throws water with the curse; the picture shows only the arm.
structure: From episode 41 (the step-up; script/ARC-41-50.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, spoken by ≤ 2.8 s; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

loop.hookQuestion: What can a new-born do against a demon?
loop.prevQuestion: What can an unborn child do against a demon?
loop.openQuestion: What does it mean to curse fire itself?

strings.recapLine: A demon in a boar's shape carried off a sage's wife.

lines.text: The child fell, shining like the sun.
lines.say: The child fell, [p:100] shining like the sun.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a statement over the image; it answers episode 41's last line at 0 s): a small child on the ground, blazing white-gold; everything else thrown into deep blue shadow. The card sits in the lower third.

lines.text: A demon, in a boar's shape, was carrying off Puloma, the sage Bhrigu's wife.
lines.say: A demon, [p:80] in a boar's shape, [p:80] was carrying off Puloma, [p:100] the sage Bhrigu's wife.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): a moment earlier: the boar running with her through the dusk (a lateral track, trunks passing).

lines.text: In fury, her unborn son dropped from her womb.
lines.say: In fury, [p:120] her unborn son [p:60] dropped from her womb.
lines.note: STORY 1: a lamp-glow match cut into the light: the child (plaque later) falls, turning, a comet of white gold; a tilt down with him.

lines.text: The demon saw him, let her go, and burned to ash.
lines.say: The demon saw him, [p:100] let her go, [p:100] and burned to ash.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT, ash (ash-grey: the colour drains): the boar's shape becomes the rakshasa's, greys, and blows away as ash on the wind; the child bright in the middle. Answers the hook.

lines.text: Puloma lifted her son and walked on, weeping.
lines.say: Puloma lifted her son [p:80] and walked on, [p:120] weeping.
lines.note: STORY 3 · NEW LIGHT (river-jade): Puloma, the child held high on her shoulder, walks small across the frame, a tear line on her cheek; above the trees, half seen in the cloud, a great calm four-faced figure looks down (Brahma sees her and comforts her: the text has it).

lines.text: Her tears became a river. Brahma himself named it: Vadhusara.
lines.say: Her tears became a river. [p:250] Brahma himself named it: [p:200] Vadhusara.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT: a crane up and back: a bright thread of water runs out behind her steps and widens into a river through the green land (plaques: Brahma · the creator; Vadhusara · "the daughter-in-law's stream"). A grace note, not the turn.
STORY 5: the hermitage: a rack focus from the new-born in the foreground to Bhrigu arriving at the gate, his water-pot in hand (plaque: Bhrigu · a great sage).

lines.speaker: bhrigu
lines.text: "Who told that demon you were my wife?"
lines.say: Who told that demon [p:120] you were my wife?
lines.note: STORY 6 · THE TURN (≈ 55 %) after a real silence · THE CLOSE-UP: a rescue becomes a hunt for someone to blame. Bhrigu's face fills the frame: relief at his son, then the brow comes down and the eyes harden; the question with a sharp turn of the head toward her. The word of the turn: WHO, clear of his face.

lines.speaker: puloma
lines.text: "The fire told him. Your son saved me."
lines.say: The fire told him. [p:300] Your son saved me.
lines.note: STORY 7: she looks toward the hut; a tilt from her hand to the household fire burning inside; then down to the child in her arms.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Her son is called Chyavana, the fallen one. Shaunaka, he is your ancestor.
lines.say: Her son is called Chyavana, [p:100] the fallen one. [p:250] Shaunaka, [p:80] he is your ancestor.
lines.note: FRAME: Sauti at the Naimisha fire, to Shaunaka, who lowers his head (plaque: Chyavana · "the fallen one"). A J-cut: the night fire first.

lines.text: Bhrigu turned to his own hearth, in a rage.
lines.say: Bhrigu turned to his own hearth, [p:120] in a rage.
lines.note: STORY 8 · NEW LIGHT (wrath-crimson, an ink bleed spreading from his figure): seen from inside the hut through the doorway: Bhrigu fills the door, the fire small between us and him.

lines.text: And Bhrigu cursed the fire itself.
lines.say: And Bhrigu [p:80] cursed the fire itself.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger): raise, then the arm thrown forward at the flames, the palm open (anticipation, action, follow-through; beard and shawl arrive late; no water: the text has only the words). The source line (top).
The NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image, with the source line; dissolve into frame 1.
